sections.name: File setup
sections.title: File setup and shared imports
sections.what: Brings in the match models and the testing tools, with a one-line description of the file.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code beyond the file description.

sections.name: match
sections.title: Builder for one process match
sections.what: Creates a valid match for a sample credit application label, with options to change the key fields so each test alters one value only.
sections.why: Likely reason: keeps each test focused on a single rule.

sections.name: result
sections.title: Builder for a whole normalisation result
sections.what: Wraps a list of matches into a result and calculates the unmatched count and mean score from them, with a fixed ontology version.
sections.why: Likely reason: produces correct summary numbers so tests do not have to work them out by hand.
sections.watch_out: Because the builder calculates its own numbers, it cannot catch a bug in those calculations. The metric tests cover that separately.

sections.name: TestMatchMethod
sections.title: Match method list is closed
sections.what: Checks that only the five allowed match methods exist (exact, alias, embedding, model, unmatched) and that any other method is rejected.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code. A closed list keeps results comparable across runs.
sections.watch_out: Adding a new method means updating this list on purpose.

sections.name: TestUnmatchedIsConsistent
sections.title: Unmatched and matched rows must agree
sections.what: A row without a canonical id must be marked unmatched, and an unmatched row must have no id. Either half alone is rejected, with messages that say so.
sections.why: The class docstring says either half alone is a service bug, and the test messages say a gap must not look like a hit.
sections.watch_out: The tests check the exact error wording, so rewording the error message will fail them.

sections.name: TestMatchScore
sections.title: Match score stays between zero and one
sections.what: Scores above one or below zero are rejected.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code beyond the valid range itself.

sections.name: TestAlternatives
sections.title: Runner-up candidates follow ordering rules
sections.what: Alternative candidates are accepted when listed best first and when none scores above the chosen match. Out-of-order lists, a higher-scoring alternative, and scores outside zero to one are rejected. Ties are allowed.
sections.why: The test docstring says the best-scoring candidate is the match, not an alternative.
sections.watch_out: Ties are accepted, so an alternative with the same score as the match is valid.

sections.name: TestMetricsCannotDrift
sections.title: Summary numbers cannot disagree with the rows
sections.what: Checks that the unmatched count and mean score must match the rows underneath them. Wrong values are rejected with a message that shows the difference. An empty result is legal, and the ontology version must not be blank.
sections.why: The class docstring says a metric that can disagree with its data looks measured when it is actually stale.
sections.watch_out: The mean check is exact to the displayed precision, so any change to how the mean is rounded needs these expectations updated.

sections.name: TestDerivedMetrics
sections.title: Match rate counts only resolved labels and no money fields
sections.what: Match rate counts only labels that resolved, not unmatched ones. The test also checks that no money-like field names (cost, savings, value and similar) exist on the result or match models.
sections.why: The docstring says these are retrieval quality measures, not money, and that nothing downstream spends them.
sections.watch_out: A future field with an innocent name such as value would fail this test even if it is harmless.

sections.name: TestImmutability
sections.title: Matches are frozen and reject unknown fields
sections.what: A match cannot be edited after it is created, and extra fields such as annual savings are rejected.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code beyond preventing edits and stopping money fields from sneaking in.
sections.watch_out: A new legitimate field must be added to the model first, or creation will fail.

sections.name: TestTheBenchmarkJoinKey
sections.title: Rules for the benchmark join key
sections.what: A row joins benchmark comparisons only when it has a canonical id and a real work unit. Unmatched rows and unspecified units are excluded. The raw label is kept next to the resolved unit.
sections.why: The docstring refers to SPEC section 2.1: free text cannot be a join key, and a bad join fails silently by showing no peers.
sections.watch_out: Changing these rules changes which processes receive peer comparisons, which can alter reports without any error.

summary: Checks the rules for matching process labels to the canonical process list, including rejected inputs, consistent summary numbers, and the join key used for benchmarks.
purpose: Protects the normalisation output, where each client process label is matched to a known process, from silent errors such as a gap that looks like a hit.
why: Each test class states its reason in a docstring. The common theme is that a wrong value should fail loudly at creation rather than surface later in a report.
how: Small helper functions build a valid match or result. Each test changes one thing and checks that the model either accepts it or rejects it with a specific message.
inputs: Hand-made match and result objects built inside the test file, plus the models in packages/schema.
outputs: Pass or fail results. No files are written.
risks: Many tests check exact wording of error messages, so harmless rewording of a message will fail tests. The match method list is fixed, so adding a method requires deliberate test changes.
debug: If a test fails with a validation error, read the message, then check the matching rule in packages/schema. If a rejection test passes but the wrong message appears, the rule may have changed for a different reason. If the metric tests fail, check how unmatched count and mean score are computed in NormalisationResult.
